stem: The marks scored by seven students in a test are: 12, 18, 9, 25, 14, 21, 16. What is the median mark?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Sorted order: 9, 12, 14, 16, 18, 21, 25. With 7 values the median is the 4th value = 16.
Computes the arithmetic mean of all 7 values: (9+12+14+16+18+21+25)/7 = 115/7 = 16.43. This uses the mean formula instead of the median definition.
Picks the 3rd value from the sorted list (14) instead of the correct middle position for n=7, which is the 4th value. This is an off-by-one error in locating the median position.
Takes the median from the unsorted list: the 4th value in the original order (25, 14, 21, 16, 18, 9, 12 re-read) is misidentified; student picks the 5th original value 18 without sorting.

explanation: Sort ascending: 9, 12, 14, 16, 18, 21, 25. n = 7 (odd). Median position = (7 + 1)/2 = 4. The 4th value in the sorted list is 16.

explanation_sections.punchline: Sort the seven values, then pick the one in the middle. The 4th position holds 16.
explanation_sections.approach: Two steps for ungrouped median: sort the data, then find the middle position. For odd n the position is (n + 1)/2 = (7 + 1)/2 = 4. Count to the 4th value in the sorted list: 9, 12, 14, 16. Do not sort inside your head; write the sorted list. If n were even, average the two middle values instead.
explanation_sections.lesson: Sort before locating the median. Picking the 4th value from the unsorted original list gives 25 (4th in original order), not 16. The sort is not optional.
explanation_sections.timing: About 40 seconds. Writing the sorted list takes 20 seconds. Position formula and count take 10 seconds. Eliminate option 3 (16.43) in five seconds: a decimal on a list of integers is the mean, not the median.
